_: THE CONCEPT VOCABULARY. Trader vernacular mapped onto canonical trees built from the closed table. DATA, not prompt text, and beside closedTable.json for the same reason: two vocabularies is the defect this repo has now paid for four times. A generic model guesses what `trending` means and guesses differently next Tuesday; this file is the FIRM'S answer, reviewable in a diff and refusable in a test.
_not_a_grammar: A CONCEPT ADDS NO NODE TYPE, NO FUNCTION AND NO NAME. Every `source` here is ordinary formula text that the ONE parser parses, the ONE linter lints and the ONE sentence module reads back. A concept is an ABBREVIATION for a tree the closed table can already express, and `ast` below is the parse result that proves it -- produced by `parse.js::parseFormula`, asserted byte-equal in `conceptVocabulary.test.js`. An example formula is a CLAIM about the table and must be PARSED, not read; three spec examples in this phase did not parse.
_expansion: A CONCEPT EXPANDS AT SAVE TIME AND THE SCAN STORES THE TREE. The word is PROVENANCE, carried beside the definition, never a late binding inside `compute.ast`. If `trending` is redefined next quarter every scan saved against today's definition keeps today's maths and today's `def_hash` -- the only reading under which a saved scan still means what its author confirmed. `version` below moves when any `source` moves, and that is an event, not a silent edit.
_grounding: EVERY CONCEPT CITES A FIRM ARTIFACT THAT ALREADY EXISTS, AND THE CITATION IS RESOLVED RATHER THAN TRUSTED. Four kinds, each looked up at check time: `filter_preset` names a preset in `api/services/screener/filters.py::FILTERS` (the firm's own labelled threshold); `starter_screen` names a shipped screen in `screener/saved_screens.py::starters()`; `scalar` names a column the screener already computes nightly and the closed table declares; `classifier` names a labelled branch of firm code, located by AST. A citation that stops resolving goes RED here rather than shipping a concept that expands into nothing.
_no_invented_numbers: ⭐ THE RAIL THAT MAKES THIS A VOCABULARY RATHER THAN AN OPINION: every numeric literal in a concept's tree must be DERIVABLE FROM ITS CITATIONS, and every scalar the tree names must be one a citation names. `rs_rank >= 80` is here because `FILTERS['rs_rank']` ships a preset labelled `Over 80`; change it to 75 and the check goes red, because 75 is nobody's published threshold. The firm's numbers, never the author's.
_refusal: AN UNGROUNDABLE WORD IS REFUSED BY NAME AND NEVER APPROXIMATED. `cheap` has no defensible definition and inventing a P/E threshold is `unmeasured accuracy claims` (spec §1.6) wearing a helpful face. The refusal says WHICH WORD it could not ground, in the concierge's existing gate-attribution style, so the member can say what they meant. A wrong scan that looks right is worse than a refusal.
_no_numbers: GROUNDING IS PROVENANCE, NOT A NUMBER. `setup_winrate` is a CLAIM subject to §1.6 and to E-6's record, and design §8.3 -- what a published record may SAY -- is OPEN. So an entry may NAME the playbook setup it is attributed to and NEVER carries a percentage. No number reaches a surface from this file.
_attribution: `attribution.setup` is a SECOND attestation, never a grounding. A playbook is prose: it can say a setup is a pullback to a rising average, but it cannot mechanically produce a tree, so it can attribute a concept and not ground one. The setup name is checked against `app/src/constants/setupGroups.js::SETUPS` on every box, and against `brain_service.lookup_playbook` on a box where the Brain Pack is installed. An uninstalled pack makes the second half unverifiable, which is reported and never patched around.
_sentence: `sentence` is `sentence.js::sentenceFor(ast)` -- DERIVED FROM THE TREE, frozen here, and asserted equal in the test. It is what a member confirms before anything is saved, and it describes the TREE rather than echoing the WORD. That is D-A5 applied to a vocabulary: the file proposes, the tree is the truth, the sentence comes from the tree.
_sentence_gap: CLOSED 2026-08-08 by `56a2bca6`, AND RECORDED BECAUSE THE HAND-OFF DEPENDED ON IT: `sentence.js::compileRules` used to build name rows from `table.series` ONLY, so a tree naming any of the table's declared SCALARS refused with `sentence:name` and 19 of the concepts below could carry no frozen sentence. `renderName` now consults the manifest's scalars section (series -> scalars -> definition inputs) and says each column in the manifest's OWN words, and `coverageGaps()` probes the walker instead of re-reading the same declaration. Every concept here is therefore renderable and every one carries a `sentence` -- each PRODUCED BY CALLING `sentenceFor(parseFormula(source).ast)`, never typed. ⛔ A hand-written sentence remains the second vocabulary this whole design exists to prevent: `conceptVocabulary.test.js` re-derives every sentence from the shipped module and refuses one the read-back would not produce, including one planted on a tree it still genuinely refuses.

trending.source: close > sma(close, 20) && sma(close, 20) > sma(close, 50) && sma(close, 50) > sma(close, 200)
trending.sentence: ((1 when close is greater than (the 20-bar average of close) and 0 otherwise) and (1 when (the 20-bar average of close) is greater than (the 50-bar average of close) and 0 otherwise)) and (1 when (the 50-bar average of close) is greater than (the 200-bar average of close) and 0 otherwise)
trending.note: The firm already answers this question every night. `screener/technicals.py` labels a symbol `full-bull` when the price is above the 20-day, the 20-day above the 50-day and the 50-day above the 200-day; `ma_stack` is a TEXT column and therefore excluded from the closed table, so the scan lane says it as a tree instead of naming the column.

in a downtrend.source: close < sma(close, 20) && sma(close, 20) < sma(close, 50) && sma(close, 50) < sma(close, 200)
in a downtrend.sentence: ((1 when close is less than (the 20-bar average of close) and 0 otherwise) and (1 when (the 20-bar average of close) is less than (the 50-bar average of close) and 0 otherwise)) and (1 when (the 50-bar average of close) is less than (the 200-bar average of close) and 0 otherwise)
in a downtrend.note: The mirror branch of the same classifier, and it is here so the vocabulary cannot only say bullish things.

leader.sentence: 1 when the relative-strength rank is greater than or equal to 80 and 0 otherwise
leader.note: 80 is the firm's own RS-rank preset, not a round number chosen here.

leaders pulling back.sentence: (((1 when the relative-strength rank is greater than or equal to 80 and 0 otherwise) and whether the price is above its 50-day average) and (1 when the percentage distance from the 20-day exponential average is greater than or equal to (the negative of 2) and 0 otherwise)) and (1 when the percentage distance from the 20-day exponential average is less than or equal to 2 and 0 otherwise)
leaders pulling back.note: The firm ships this screen. Every term is one of its three filters, at its thresholds.

coiled.sentence: whether the recent bars are tightly consolidated
coiled.note: The column IS the concept: `screener/candles.py` sets it when the ten-close coefficient of variation is under 2.5%. The word is the English name for a number the screener already computes.

tight base.sentence: (1 when the relative-strength rank is greater than or equal to 80 and 0 otherwise) and whether the recent bars are tightly consolidated
tight base.note: The firm's shipped `High-RS tight bases` screen, term for term.

oversold.sentence: 1 when the nightly 14-period RSI is less than or equal to 30 and 0 otherwise
oversold.note: The threshold and the word both come from the firm's own preset label.

overbought.sentence: 1 when the nightly 14-period RSI is greater than or equal to 70 and 0 otherwise

heavy volume.sentence: 1 when the volume ratio against its own average is greater than or equal to 2 and 0 otherwise
heavy volume.note: Two times the symbol's own average, which is the higher of the two volume presets the firm ships.

liquid.sentence: 1 when the 30-day average volume is greater than or equal to 1000000 and 0 otherwise

gapping up.sentence: 1 when the opening gap percentage is greater than or equal to 3 and 0 otherwise

gapping down.sentence: 1 when the opening gap percentage is less than or equal to (the negative of 3) and 0 otherwise

near its highs.sentence: 1 when the percentage distance from the 52-week high is greater than or equal to (the negative of 5) and 0 otherwise
near its highs.note: `dist_52w_high_pct` is negative below the high, so `within 5%` is `>= -5` and not `<= 5`. Getting that backwards is the sign error a read-back exists to surface.

at the 20 ema.sentence: (1 when the percentage distance from the 20-day exponential average is greater than or equal to (the negative of 2) and 0 otherwise) and (1 when the percentage distance from the 20-day exponential average is less than or equal to 2 and 0 otherwise)
at the 20 ema.note: The firm's preset is a BAND (`between -2 and 2`), so the expansion is two comparisons rather than one.

shallow pullback.sentence: 1 when the depth of the current pullback is less than or equal to 10 and 0 otherwise

deep pullback.sentence: 1 when the depth of the current pullback is greater than or equal to 20 and 0 otherwise

higher lows.sentence: 1 when the run of consecutive higher lows is greater than or equal to 3 and 0 otherwise

closing strong.sentence: 1 when the close's position inside the bar's range is greater than or equal to 0.66 and 0 otherwise

at new highs.sentence: whether the bar made a new 52-week high

large cap.sentence: 1 when the market capitalisation is greater than or equal to 10000000000 and 0 otherwise

mega cap.sentence: 1 when the market capitalisation is greater than or equal to 200000000000 and 0 otherwise

_refused_why: EACH REASON NAMES THE WORD, because a member who is refused needs to know which of their words could not be ground -- not that `something` failed. These are words a member will plausibly say and this vocabulary deliberately declines to guess at.

_refused.cheap: "cheap" has no defensible definition here. The firm's own screen that uses the word -- `Cheap quality compounders` -- bundles a forward-P/E ceiling with an ROE floor and an EPS-growth floor, so the word alone does not say which multiple you mean, or whether quality is part of it. Say `forward P/E under 20`, or name the screen.
_refused.expensive: "expensive" is the mirror of `cheap` and has the same problem: no single multiple is the firm's answer, and picking one would be somebody's opinion presented as the house view.
_refused.strong: "strong" is ambiguous between three different scans -- relative strength (`rs_rank`), price momentum (`chg_pct_1w` / `chg_pct_1m`) and fundamental quality (`uct_composite`). Name which one and the vocabulary can ground it.
_refused.quality: "quality" is not one measure. `roe`, `op_margin`, `net_margin` and `uct_composite` are four different screens and the firm has never declared one of them to be the definition.
_refused.momentum: "momentum" has no published threshold in this codebase. There are one-day, one-week and one-month change columns and no preset on any of them, so any cut-off would be invented here rather than read from the firm's own screens.
_refused.small cap: "small cap" cannot be ground: the only market-cap preset in that direction is a FLOOR (`Small+ (>$300M)`), and there is no upper bound anywhere in the repo to read. A band would be this file's opinion, not the firm's.
_refused.undervalued: "undervalued" is a claim about fair value, and nothing in this codebase computes one. Refusing is the honest answer; a P/E rule dressed as a valuation verdict is not.
